title: Contract a given semistable modification to a stable one
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. Suppose a semistable $\eta$-modification $(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ is given. Then it factors through a stable $\eta$-modification $(X^{\mathrm{st}},D^{\mathrm{st}})\to(X,D)$; the factor map $(Y,E)\to(X^{\mathrm{st}},D^{\mathrm{st}})$ is an $\eta$-modification. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.6 and its successive exceptional blow-down construction, pp. 32--33; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED (see report.md).

proof.text: First the generic fibre of every flat $T$-scheme occurring here is a schematically dense open. If $V$ is a field this is the whole scheme. Otherwise choose a nonzero $a$ in the smallest nonzero prime ideal of $V$. Every nonzero prime contains $a$, hence $D(a)=\{(0)\}=\eta$ in $T$ and $V[1/a]=K$. By the stalkwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the tensor-injectivity definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], multiplication by $a$ is injective on each local ring: tensor the injection $V_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{a}V_{\mathfrak p}$. It is therefore injective on sections on any affine open. Localization of its coordinate ring at $a$ is injective, proving $\mathcal O_Z\hookrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_{Z_\eta}$. This applies also to every marking, including the empty one.

source.place: Elementary verification of schematic density from the stated flatness hypotheses

proof.text: For a semistable modification $f$ of the fixed target $(X,D)$, use [lem-trf-valuation-exceptional-closed-image-criterion] to form the finite set $B_f$ of fibre-component generic points whose images are closed in $X$. Prove the desired factorization by strong induction on $N=|B_f|$, simultaneously for all such $f$ with this fixed target. If $f$ is stable, the identity on $(Y,E)$ gives the factorization and is an $\eta$-modification. In particular $N=0$ is this case by the same criterion.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4 and Proposition 4.4.6 proof, printed pp. 31--32

proof.text: If $f$ is not stable, [lem-trf-valuation-exceptional-closed-image-criterion] supplies an exceptional $z\in B_f$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-exceptional-blowdown] to obtain $h:(Y,E)\to(Y_1,E_1)$ and a semistable $f_1:(Y_1,E_1)\to(X,D)$ with $f_1h=f$. Its explicit bijection gives $|B_{f_1}|=N-1<N$. The target, valuation ring and smooth generic target are unchanged, so all induction hypotheses apply to $f_1$. We obtain a stable $g:(X^{\mathrm{st}},D^{\mathrm{st}})\to(X,D)$ and an $\eta$-modification $q:(Y_1,E_1)\to(X^{\mathrm{st}},D^{\mathrm{st}})$ with $gq=f_1$. Thus $g(qh)=f$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4, Lemma 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.4.6 proof, printed pp. 31--33

proof.text: The curve and marking maps of $qh$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a), since both factors are proper on both parts. Their generic fibres are composites of isomorphisms. By step 1 the generic fibres are schematically dense opens in both the source pair and the resulting stable pair; $qh$ is an isomorphism over these opens. It is therefore an $\eta$-modification in the precise sense of the item. This completes the strong induction and the required factorization.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.6 conclusion, printed pp. 32--33; properness and schematic-density verification

lean.statement: theorem valuation_semistable_stable_contraction (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] (V : ValuationSubring K) [Finite (PrimeSpectrum V)] (X Y : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (hX : Smooth (pullback.snd X.x (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (hD : Etale (pullback.snd X.d (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)))) (f : Y.Hom X) (hf : f.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype))) (hY : Y.IsSemistable) : ∃ (Z : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (g : Z.Hom X) (q : Y.Hom Z), g.IsStable (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) ∧ q.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.toSubring.subtype)) ∧ q.curve ≫ g.curve = f.curve ∧ q.marking ≫ g.marking = f.marking
